Q5607422.label: 1995 Grenadian general election
Q5607422.desc: General elections in Grenada held on 20 June 1995
Q5607422.summary: General elections were held in Grenada on 20 June 1995. The result was a victory for the New National Party, which won eight of the 15 seats. Voter turnout was 62%.

Q57342.label: Mauricio Funes
Q57342.desc: President of El Salvador from 2009 to 2014
Q57342.summary: Carlos Mauricio Funes Cartagena was a Salvadoran politician and journalist who served as the 41st president of El Salvador from 2009 to 2014. Funes won the 2009 presidential election as the candidate of the left-wing Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front (FMLN).

Q84081662.label: 2023 Monegasque parliamentary election
Q84081662.summary: General elections were held in Monaco on 5 February 2023. The result was a landslide victory for the governing Monegasque National Union led by Brigitte Boccone-Pagès, which won all 24 seats on the National Council. The new council was sworn in on 16 February.

Q123902.label: Ruth Dreifuss
Q123902.summary: Ruth Dreifuss is a Swiss economist, unionist and politician who served as a member of the Federal Council from 1993 to 2002. She served as Vice President of Switzerland in 1998 and as President of Switzerland in 1999 for the Social Democratic Party.

Q7209982.label: 2010 Polish Senate by-elections
Q7209982.summary: Three by-elections to the Senate were held in Poland on 20 June 2010, at the same time as the presidential election. They were held to replace Krystyna Bochenek in Katowice, Janina Fetlińska in Płock and Stanisław Zając in Krosno, who died in the 2010 Polish Air Force Tu-154 crash on 10 April 2010.

Q636414.label: 1990 Hungarian parliamentary election
Q636414.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 25 March 1990, with a second round of voting taking place in all but five single member constituencies on 8 April. They were the first completely free and competitive elections to be held in the country since 1945, and only the second completely free elections with universal suffrage in the country's history.

Q2601982.label: 2009 Albanian parliamentary election
Q2601982.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Albania on 28 June 2009. No alliance achieved 71 deputies on its own needed to form a parliamentary majority. A coalition government was formed by the Democratic Party and Socialist Movement for Integration.

Q16959998.label: 1940 Latvian parliamentary election
Q16959998.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Latvia on 14 and 15 July 1940, alongside simultaneous elections in Estonia and Lithuania, following the Soviet occupation of the three countries. The Communist Party of Latvia was legalised, and it created the "Latvian Working People's Bloc" to take part in the elections. It was the only organization allowed to stand in the elections; an attempt to include the Democratic Bloc, an alliance of all now-banned Latvian parties except the Social Democratic Workers' Party, on the ballot was suppressed.

Q1604094.label: 1939 Turkish general election
Q1604094.desc: general election held in the Republic of Turkey in 1939
Q1604094.summary: General elections were held in Turkey on 26 March 1939. The Republican People's Party was the only party in the country at the time. Voter turnout was reported to be 77.8%.

Q11774.label: Gupta Empire
Q11774.desc: ancient Indian empire (c. 3rd century CE–575 CE)
Q11774.summary: The Gupta Empire was an Indian empire during the classical period of the Indian subcontinent which existed from the mid 3rd century to mid 6th century CE. At its peak, the dynasty ruled over an empire that spanned much of the northern Indian subcontinent. This period has been considered as the Golden Age of India by some historians, although this characterisation has been disputed by others. The ruling dynasty of the empire was founded by Gupta.
